themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 5 this week, a 264% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.4 per week, marking a sudden acceleration in vandalism across Lower Manhattan that warrants investigation into whether this reflects organized activity or a broader deterioration in street conditions.
evidence: 5 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.65)
264% spike over baseline — statistically significant deviation
Concentrated in single reporting period, suggesting potential localized or organized activity
reporting_angles: Are particular neighborhoods or blocks being targeted; visual documentation of affected areas
Community perception of deterioration — is graffiti cleanup responsive or are complaints outpacing removal?

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster this week
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints doubled this week to 4 cases versus the 1.8 weekly average, a 129% spike (z-score: 3.4) that suggests either a localized foodborne illness incident or emerging restaurant hygiene violations in Lower Manhattan requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.4)
129% spike — statistically significant deviation suggesting acute outbreak or pattern
Potential public health emergency if cases are clustered by source restaurant or food type
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Dept. to determine if complaints point to single food source or multiple establishments
Interview affected residents to identify common restaurants or food vendors; cross-reference with DOH inspection records

themes_detail.label: Encampment surge last week
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints exploded to 69 last week, a 411% increase over the 8-week baseline of 13.5 per week (z-score: 4.47), indicating a rapid worsening of homeless encampment visibility or concentration in Lower Manhattan that aligns with long-standing community board requests for public health interventions.
evidence: 69 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.47)
411% spike — most severe statistical deviation in dataset
Converges with persistent community board budget request for 'public health issues programs' (year-over-year ask), suggesting chronic underlying problem now accelerating
reporting_angles: Map encampment hotspots — are they concentrated in parks, subway areas, or streets; visual documentation of conditions
Interview outreach workers, community leaders, and affected residents about triggers for sudden spike and availability of shelter/services
Investigate whether city shelter capacity constraints or policy changes are driving street encampments

themes_detail.label: Air quality deterioration last week
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints surged 260% last week to 9 cases versus the 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.81), a sudden spike that may reflect episodic pollution, construction dust, or industrial emissions requiring environmental investigation and resident notification.
evidence: 9 air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.81)
260% spike — second-highest statistical deviation in dataset
Likely tied to specific event or source (e.g., major construction, industrial incident, weather inversion)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with EPA/DEC air quality monitoring data and DOB construction permits (1186 filed in last 90 days, 1013 alterations) to identify pollution source
Interview residents about visibility, odors, respiratory symptoms; contact environmental justice advocates

themes_detail.label: Outdoor dining enforcement surge last week
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked 500% last week to 3 cases from a baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score: 3.54), suggesting either enforcement action against unpermitted sidewalk dining operations or emerging resident complaints about encroachment on public space in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.54)
500% spike from historically low baseline — significant proportional increase
May reflect post-pandemic normalization of street dining or enforcement crackdown on unpermitted operations
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects vendor enforcement action or resident complaints about blocked sidewalks/hygiene
Interview affected restaurant owners and community members about permit status and accessibility disputes
